edges.allele: lof^dt2: gain of function; inversion with breakpoints at 23.174 Mb (upstream of prrx1a) and 24.075 Mb (between kcc4a and kcnh2a) in Zv11
edges.consistency_check: the 24.075 Mb breakpoint lies about 5.6 kb upstream of the ZFIN GRCz11 start of kcnh2a (24,080,694), as 'between kcc4a and kcnh2a' implies; the paper gives Mb to three decimals
edges.effect: ectopic kcnh2a expression drives fin overgrowth
edges.evidence_class: causal_intervention (as reported: mutants, cis revertants, overexpression)

edges.allele: nr21 (dmh26), T200K, dominant; cis frameshift revertant L106Rfs39; lat4a^del (mh152)
edges.consequence: lat4a is not shown to be REQUIRED for normal fin length; only the gain-of-function allele has an effect
edges.effect: nr21 shortens all fins without a statistically decreased body size; the revertants show nr21 acts by gain of function; lat4a null has no fin phenotype
lat4a nr21 suppresses the overgrowth caused by lof in the median fins and leaves elongated paired fins plus a hypocercal caudal fin: a fin-proportion pattern like flying fishes
edges.mechanism: kcnh2a expression does not change with nr21 (qRT-PCR) and the paper concludes the suppression acts downstream of bioelectric signalling; the mechanism is not identified

genomes_available_is_not_a_mutation_map.why: the 35-species data are pooled targeted capture of conserved regions (average 78.3% of targeted regions at 38.3-fold), the F326L link is a correlation the authors themselves caveat, and F326L (natural, flying fishes) is a different residue from T200K (laboratory, zebrafish); no flying-fish variant is shown to change fin length

phylogenomic_links.observation: a shared lat4a F326L substitution across lineages with enlarged pectoral fins
lat4a elevated evolutionary rate in gliding lineages and phyloP acceleration at the flying-fish ancestor
one flying fish lacks the convergent lat4a allele and has an elongated dorsal fin

what_is_not: flight or gliding performance (no aerodynamic or locomotion measurement in zebrafish appears in the text read)
the flying-fish genotype: the zebrafish alleles (lat4a T200K, kcnh2a lof inversion) are not the flying-fish variants
that flying fishes use these two genes: the genomic data are correlational
